result.title: Adversarial Robustness of Kernel Machines: A Comprehensive Analysis
result.summary: Kernel machines are an important class of models in machine learning. However, the question of how robust modern kernel machines are to adversarial examples has not been studied comprehensively. In this paper, we provide a thorough empirical investigation of the adversarial robustness of kernel-based models for both binary and multiclass classification tasks, via white-box and black-box evasion attacks. We evaluate the native robustness of kernel machines, random feature classifiers, and the relatively newer Recursive Feature Machines. In addition, we provide an algorithm for approximate adversarial training of kernel machines. Our experiments on classification tasks on image and tabular datasets strongly indicate that kernel machines are natively more robust than neural networks, i.e., their performance degrades more gracefully against adversarial perturbations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文对核机器（含随机特征分类器与 Recursive Feature Machines）在二分类与多分类图像、表格任务上的对抗鲁棒性做系统实证评估，涵盖白盒与黑盒逃逸攻击，并提出一种近似对抗训练算法。
